option_relations.rationale: Option A describes infection-related glomerulonephritis secondary to LVAD-associated Corynebacterium jeikeium infection, which is a broader category encompassing the more specific immune-complex crescentic glomerulonephritis mentioned in the leaf.

Option B, 'Focal segmental necrotising immune-complex glomerulonephritis triggered by chronic LVAD infection with Corynebacterium jeikeium', is clinically equivalent to the leaf 'LVAD-associated infection (Corynebacterium jeikeium bacteremia) causing immune-complex crescentic glomerulonephritis (post-infectious glomerulonephritis)'. Both describe the same underlying pathology and etiology.

While membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis can be infection-related, the biopsy findings specifically describe focal segmental necrotizing and crescentic changes with immune complex deposits, not typical membranoproliferative patterns.

While there is an LVAD infection, the primary diagnosis in the leaf is glomerulonephritis, not infective endocarditis, although endocarditis could be a source of the infection leading to glomerulonephritis, it is not the direct diagnosis of the renal pathology.
